examples: *The manager insisted that he **appease** the angry customer.* (insist that + base form)
*It is **vital that** every leader **be** approachable.* (no -s, even with every person)
*The minister proposed that the plan **achieve economic growth** within a year.* (propose that)
*The lawyer suggested that the report **not contain** any home truths.* (negative: not + base form)
*If I **were** you, I would not repeat that home truth.* (unreal: were for all persons)
***Be that as it may**, we still need a decision.* (fixed phrase)
grammar.explanation:
The **subjunctive** is a verb form for things **demanded, suggested or necessary**, not facts. It always uses the **base form** of the verb, for every person: *The manager insisted that he **appease** the angry client.* (not *appeases*)

It follows **that**-clauses after verbs like **insist, suggest, demand, recommend, propose** and adjectives like **essential, vital, crucial**: *It is **vital that** every leader **be** approachable.* Notice — no *-s*, even with *he / she / it*.

Negatives put **not** before the base form: *The lawyer suggested that the report **not contain** any home truths.* The passive works too: *It is **essential that** the plan **be approved** before we try to achieve economic growth.*

For unreal situations, use **were** for every person: *If I **were** you, I would not repeat that home truth.* And the old fixed phrases survive in modern English: **be that as it may**, **come what may**, **if need be**, **so be it**.

Common mistake: never add **to** or **-s**. Say *I suggest that he **pay*** — never *pays* or *to pay*. British English often uses *should* instead: *…that he **should pay***.

practice.a: The CEO demanded that the team be approachable.
practice.q: The CEO wanted the team to be approachable. (use: demanded that)

practice.a: It is essential that we have the time of our lives on holiday.
practice.q: It is very important that we have the time of our lives on holiday. (use: essential that)

practice.a: The manager recommended that she not share the home truth with the press.
practice.q: The manager asked her not to share the home truth with the press. (use: recommended that)

practice.a: Come what may, the board will hire an altruistic director.
practice.q: The board wants to hire an altruistic director, and nothing will stop them. (use: come what may)
